mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares the nature of images formed when the magnification (m) is +2 and when it is -0.5 for a spherical mirror?

options.A: +2 gives an upright, magnified, virtual image; -0.5 gives an inverted, reduced, real image.
options.B: +2 gives an inverted, reduced, real image; -0.5 gives an upright, magnified, virtual image.
options.C: +2 gives a virtual image behind the mirror; -0.5 gives a real image at the pole of the mirror.
options.D: +2 gives a real image at the centre of curvature; -0.5 gives a virtual image at the focal point.

mcqs.answer: +2 gives an upright, magnified, virtual image; -0.5 gives an inverted, reduced, real image.
mcqs.explanation: For spherical mirrors, magnification m = -v/u. A positive m indicates an upright (virtual) image, while a negative m indicates an inverted (real) image. Hence m = +2 corresponds to an upright, magnified, virtual image, and m = -0.5 corresponds to an inverted, reduced, real image. The other options mix up the sign‑interpretation.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of the mirror. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what are the image distance (v) and the magnification (m)?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave mirror, f = -15 cm and u = -30 cm. Mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = -1/15 + 1/30 = -1/30, so v = -30 cm (real image). Magnification m = -v/u = -(-30)/-30 = -1, indicating an inverted image of the same size. The other options result from incorrect sign handling or arithmetic errors.

mcqs.question: The mirror formula that relates object distance (u), image distance (v) and focal length (f) for a spherical mirror is:
mcqs.explanation: The standard mirror formula derived from geometry of spherical mirrors is 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where all distances are taken with the Cartesian sign convention. Option B is the lens formula, while C and D are not correct relationships for mirrors.

mcqs.question: According to the Cartesian sign convention for mirrors, which of the following statements is correct for a convex mirror?

options.A: The focal length is taken as positive.
options.B: The object distance is taken as positive.
options.C: The image distance is taken as negative.

mcqs.answer: The focal length is taken as positive.
mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured against the direction of incident light are negative. For a convex mirror, the centre of curvature lies behind the mirror, so the focal length (and radius) are taken as positive. Object distance is always negative, image distance for a convex mirror is positive, and magnification can be positive or negative depending on the situation, so only option A is correct.

mcqs.question: When the mirror formula yields a positive image distance (v) for a spherical mirror, the image is:

options.A: Real and formed in front of the mirror
options.B: Virtual and formed behind the mirror
options.C: Located at the pole of the mirror

mcqs.answer: Virtual and formed behind the mirror
mcqs.explanation: A positive image distance for mirrors indicates that the image lies on the same side as the reflected rays, i.e., behind the mirror, which is the definition of a virtual image. A real image would have a negative v. Hence option B is correct.

mcqs.question: A convex mirror has a focal length of +20 cm. An object is placed 40 cm in front of the mirror. What is the magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Using the sign convention: f = +20 cm, u = -40 cm. Mirror formula gives 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/20 + 1/40 = 3/40, so v = 40/3 cm ≈ 13.33 cm (positive, virtual). Magnification m = -v/u = -13.33 / -40 = +0.33. Positive magnification indicates an upright, reduced image. The other options arise from sign mistakes.

mcqs.question: An object placed 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm forms an image with magnification -0.5. Which description best matches the image?
mcqs.explanation: Negative magnification indicates an inverted image. The magnitude |m| = 0.5 means the image height is half that of the object, i.e., reduced. For a concave mirror, an inverted image is real. Therefore option B correctly describes the image. Options A and C incorrectly state the image is upright, and D incorrectly states it is magnified.

mcqs.question: A dentist uses a concave mirror of focal length 8 cm to examine a tooth. He holds the mirror so that the tooth (object) is 12 cm from the mirror. Determine (i) the image distance and (ii) the nature and size of the image formed.

options.A: Image distance = -24 cm; real, inverted, magnified 2×
options.B: Image distance = +24 cm; virtual, upright, reduced 0.5×
options.C: Image distance = -6 cm; real, inverted, reduced 0.5×
options.D: Image distance = +6 cm; virtual, upright, magnified 2×

mcqs.answer: Image distance = -24 cm; real, inverted, magnified 2×
mcqs.explanation: Using sign convention: f = -8 cm, u = -12 cm. Mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = -1/8 + 1/12 = -1/24, so v = -24 cm (real image in front of mirror). Magnification m = -v/u = -(-24)/-12 = -2, indicating the image is inverted and twice the size of the object (magnified). Option A matches these results; the other options contain incorrect signs or magnitude.
